/ Concerning Transmigration. /
Mani explains that although both sinners and catechumens must pass into transmigration, the fate of these two categories differs. He compares this to the educative punishment that must on occasion be meted out to erring children, contrasted with that imposed on wicked servants. Thus the catechumens will in the end attain to the light and the life, while sinners will be imprisoned and suffer eternal death.
[Once again o]ne of the catechumens questioned the apost/ [le. He says] to him: We have heard a lesson from you, my master.
